contract_conflicts.observation: The O01 manifest requires mandatory lanes to be class-aware, but no authoritative E0-E5 to mandatory-lane matrix exists.
QueryPlan has no work-class or EpistemicWorkClassification ID, revision, input hash, or classification hash binding, while required_lanes accepts arbitrary strings.
SearchLaneReceipt defines counterevidence, but retrieval policy and workflow use counter; no authoritative alias or migration rule exists.
SearchCompletenessCertificate required/completed/blocked lanes accept arbitrary strings, and its canonical example uses support even though support is not a SearchLaneReceipt lane.

The workflow executes eleven retrieval nodes and always requires all eleven receipts, while the O01 exit criterion says mandatory lanes are class-aware; no selected, applicable, waived, or intentionally unselected semantics reconciles those statements.

SearchLaneReceipt requires non-empty query text, a query hash, scope, corpus hash, index versions, and timestamps even for UNSEARCHED, but no rule defines truthful values for an intentionally unselected lane.
No canonical mapping defines whether provider_failure, policy_blocked, budget exhaustion, time exhaustion, or manual stop produces PARTIAL, BLOCKED, lane failure, or run failure.
The architecture uses whenever-applicable language but provides no typed applicability input, decision artifact, authority, waiver vocabulary, non-waivable floor, or deterministic evaluator.

Support is used as an evidence role and certificate lane, while lexical and semantic are retrieval mechanisms; no authoritative role-to-lane mapping says whether support is a lane, a projection, or a result label.
